obs: "The Murdock opinion recognizes, p. 394, that the word \"willful\" often denotes an intentional as distinguished from an accidental act."
“The general rule is that willfulness does not require knowledge of illegality”
Jerman v. Carlisle, McNellie, Rini, Kramer & Ulrich, L.P.A.
"although 'willfully is a word of many meanings dependent on context'"

“[W]e note that the automatic stay provision uses the word ‘willful,’ a word the law typically does not associate with strict liability but “ 'whose construction is often dependent on the context in which it appears.' ””
"with respect to federal crimes requiring willfulness, the Court generally requires the Government to prove that the defendant was aware that his conduct was unlawful."
